object_context: After quotienting witness-local Theorem-24 propagation by the antecedent-membership congruence, audit the source-defined global cover-incidence object itself. Determine whether exact equivalence of semi-filters by their pair-cover neighborhoods exposes a noncanonical coordinate that survives known cheap/canonical controls before any scalar lower-bound invariant is proposed.
structural_coordinates: Cavalar-Oliveira cover complexity rho(A,B) is the minimum number of pair vertices whose cover-graph neighborhoods hit every relevant semi-filter vertex.
The cover graph has pair vertices (E,H) with E,H subsets of U=A^c and semi-filter vertices F above some a in A; (E,H) covers F iff E,H are in F and E intersect H is not in F.
Theorem 30 exactly identifies rho(A,B) with cyclic intersection complexity, so any global cover-incidence quotient must preserve the set-cover problem rather than merely correlate with it.
O9d12a2a1a1a showed fixed-Lambda witness-local propagation is determined by the base empty-set flag plus individual E_i/H_i membership bits, pruning hidden recurrence state.

For G_NEQ, Proposition 40 gives full cover complexity equal to canonical cover complexity equal to log N; therefore any noncanonical global state that explodes on G_NEQ but does not alter the cover neighborhoods needed for the optimum is a hostile calibration, not hardness.

All-rectangle generator families can have rho=0 because a singleton generator above a target element forces the empty trace, leaving no semi-filter above that element; raw state-count measures must therefore vanish or fail closed there.

A pair-neighborhood quotient identifies semi-filters F,F' when the set of pair vertices covering F equals the set covering F'; deleting duplicate rows under this equivalence preserves the exact set-cover optimum by construction.
No count, entropy, rank, depth, width or quotient-size scalar is authorized until a bounded per-pair accounting law and hard-target bridge are proved.
